learningObjective: Identify which fusions are standard in production LLM inference stacks and what each fusion saves.

canonicalClaims.claim: Production LLM stacks fuse: QKV projection (one wide GEMM); RMSNorm (or as GEMM-input epilogue); SwiGLU (silu*up elementwise); attention (FlashAttention/PagedAttention keeps S on-chip); sampling (temperature + top-k/top-p).
conditions: Modern data-center GPU with tensor cores.
Model uses recognizable patterns (SwiGLU, RMSNorm, MHA/GQA).
nonImplications: Does not imply zero remaining HBM roundtrips.

misconceptions.claim: Full transformer block is fused into one kernel per layer in production.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Full-block fusion is a research direction; production uses targeted fusion.

misconceptions.claim: Modern GPUs' launch overhead is negligible for LLM decode.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Decode has many small kernels; per-kernel launch overhead is a significant fraction and motivates CUDA Graphs.

misconceptions.claim: The entire model can be fused into one hardware kernel.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Hardware kernels are bounded by resource constraints; this is impractical.

implementationFacts: FlashAttention/PagedAttention is the biggest single fusion win in LLM decode.
Sampling fusion combines softmax with temperature and top-k/top-p in a single kernel.
performanceScenarios: The fusion set materially reduces HBM roundtrips of intermediates and kernel launch overhead in decode.
